verdict.reasoning: Patient says, 'I keep having a headache' and 'It started yesterday,' indicating new-onset headache since yesterday.

Location: 'It's on the left side at the back'; character: 'quite, intense, and kinda quite throbbing'; onset: 'About mid-morning' and 'It kind of built up gradually'; severity: 'I'd say about eight' on a 0–10 scale.

Diurnal pattern: 'Has it been worse at any particular time of the day?' – 'No'; positional/Valsalva: 'Any difference if you lie down, stand up, bend over, cough or sneeze, or anything like that?' – 'Um, no.'
Patient states, 'I took some Nurofen, yesterday' and when asked if it helped: 'Not really,' indicating ibuprofen provided no relief.
'Have you got any other medical problems?' – 'Um, no I haven't'; 'And any stomach problems, or asthma at all?' – 'No'; prior headache: 'in the past, have you had any headache before?' – 'Not really.'
'Anything you take medication for?' – 'No I don't'; 'any over-the-counter medications' – 'No, only the, Nurofen I took yesterday, Ibuprofen.'
Doctor asks about 'any over-the-counter medications or allergies?' but the patient only answers about Nurofen; no explicit statement of having no drug allergies is given.
Family history: 'Anyone in your family got any medical problems?' – 'my mother's had hypertension, and she does get migraines.'

Living situation: 'Who do you live with at home?' – 'My partner'; job: 'What's your job, day-to-day?' – 'I'm a designer'; smoking: 'do you smoke at all normally?' – 'No I don't'; alcohol: 'Do you drink any alcohol regularly?' – 'No'; drugs: 'any other drugs?' – 'No.'
Work: 'Have you had to miss any work at all?' – 'Uh, no'; function: 'I don't feel that, I'm finding it really hard to, to do any of, my work, or, normal things.'

Acute, unilateral, severe left occipital headache: 'It's on the left side at the back'; severe and gradual: 'quite, intense... throbbing... built up gradually'; first episode: 'in the past, have you had any headache before?' – 'Not really'; poor response to ibuprofen: 'did that make any difference?' – 'Not really'; family history migraine: 'she does get migraines'; red flags denied: no fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, visual changes, or neurologic symptoms were reported.
Doctor: 'we would suggest is, trying a slightly stronger, pain relief. Uh, so, similar to Ibuprofen, but taking instead of Ibuprofen... and taking that regularly with food.'
Doctor: 'You can take Paracetamol along with that.' indicating concurrent paracetamol use.
Doctor: 'Try and um, take rest, have lots of good hydration.'
Doctor: 'if the pain's getting worse, or you get new symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness... or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing, then we need to speak to you.'

Doctor: 'Well I should think it should down, if it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two. Then certainly give us a call back, if, when you've tried the medication that I've prescribed.'
